reason: This is a hypothesis ranking, not a measured-performance ranking. I put small changes to the active K loop first: they keep the current layout and FP32 update order, with limited bounds risk. Prefetching is next because the supplied cache-line and L1D facts make it testable, though earlier prefetch advice regressed on the inactive path and does not predict this result. Scratch blocking may reduce reserved space, but adds loop work. B layouts and transpose fusion have greater potential to change data access, but add timed packing or require a more complex active-path rewrite; the per-panel packing proposal may repeat work under the current row-band traversal. Padding has no supplied evidence of a cache conflict and increases footprint. The general-path transpose proposal does not affect the fixed n=512 timing and its direct-consumption layout is underspecified.
